equity.level_reason: Coverage is reported by county SVI tertile and the Discussion links lower coverage in high-SVI counties to cost and billing barriers, but SVI values are only set side by side (e.g., 33.6% vs 27.4%) with no computed difference or ratio, so the cap at 2 applies.

level_alternative.reason: The SVI gradient is framed as barriers that 'disproportionately affect' under-resourced nursing homes, with cost and Medicare Part D billing named as structural explanations.

notes: Design inferred as surveillance/descriptive; none named. Comparisons with 2023 coverage and NIS adult coverage in the Discussion use unpublished or cited data and are context. Representativeness of voluntary reporters was judged by comparing distributions side by side, with no test.
view_issues: In the CSV, the RSV facility-size rows shift 'No. of residents' into the blank column, so the later RSV values sit one column off. The prepass 'prevalence_ratio' cue is a false hit on the abbreviation 'PR'.
